newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Komercni rejects Raiffeisen report. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Czech Komercni rejects Raiffeisen report. [CORRECTED 16:00 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects name of institution issuing report throughout from Raiffeisen Bank to Raiffeisen Capital and Investment s.r.o.)

Komercni Banka a.s., the largest Czech commercial bank, sharply criticised the findings of a report by Raiffeisen Capital and Investment s.r.o. which said Komercni was massively underprovisioned and that its shares were heavily overvalued.

In a statement issued to Reuters on Thursday, Komercni said Raiffeisen Capital and Investment's analysis was contradicted by the bank's annual report which was conducted to international accounting standards by Arthur Anderson.

"Raiffeisen (Capital and Investment's) analysis that there are insufficient reserves to cover potential losses on Komercni's loans is fundamentally at variance with the statment of renowned international auditing firm Arthur Anderson," Komercni said.
"(Arthur Anderson's) statement this year, for the third time in a row, was made 'without objections'," it added.
Raiffeisen Capital and Investment, in a report issued in mid-May, alleged that Komercni may be more than 40 billion crowns short of being suffiently provisioned.

"Komercni Banka is significantly under-provisioned. We estimate that at least CZK 8.5 billion in provisions are needed immediately, and that another 32 billion would be necessary if the bank were to provision by U.S. standards," the report said.

The report concluded that under an optimistic scenario which assumed that 75 percent of the estimated collatoral backing loss loans was recoverable, Komercni's share price should fall to 1,450 crowns from the current 1,990.
But it added: "A more realistic scenario which assumes that only 50 percent of the collateral can be collected, values the bank at approximately CZK 900-1,000 per share."

However, Komercni's rebuttal also noted that the Czech bank had received investment grade ratings from three of the world's leading rating agencies and that the quality of the loan portfolio had been thoroughly assessed in the rating process.

"In March 1996 Moody's gave (Komercni) a long term Baa2 rating and a short term Prime-2. In April of the same year we got a long term IBCA rating of A- and a short term A2 and in January 1997 the bank got a Standard and Poor's rating of BBB- long term and A3 short term," komercni's statement said.

"In analysing Komercni in the process of the ratings, the question of the quality of the loan portfolio and the level of reserves were among the most important aspects considered. (Both areas) were judged to be sufficient," it added.
